problem: Keep a very large codebase maintainable and productive for developers.
title: Shopify modularises its Rails monolith instead of moving to microservices
context: Shopify's core monolith had over 2.8 million lines of Ruby code and 500,000 commits.
decision_made: Componentise the monolith with enforced boundaries instead of splitting into microservices, because of the complexity of distributed systems.
action_taken: Started componentisation around 2017 and released the Packwerk boundary-checking tool in September 2020.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used. Shopify later wrote a retrospective on Packwerk.
lessons: Enforced module boundaries can bring some benefits of microservices without distributed-system costs.
limitations: Only excerpts of Shopify's posts were seen. Packwerk's privacy checks were later removed, and results on developer productivity were not verified.

claims.claim_text: Shopify chose a modular monolith over microservices because of the complexity of distributed systems.
Shopify released the Packwerk tool for enforcing boundaries between packages of Ruby files in 2020.
